stem: An asymptomatic 45-year-old adult at average risk for colorectal cancer has never been screened. What does the current USPSTF recommendation support?

options.A: Defer routine screening until age 60 because average-risk adults younger than 60 do not benefit.
options.B: Wait for gastrointestinal symptoms before screening because asymptomatic adults do not meet screening criteria.
options.C: Begin colorectal cancer screening now using one of the USPSTF-recommended screening strategies.
options.D: Begin annual colonoscopy now because colonoscopy every year is the preferred USPSTF screening strategy.

rationale: The current USPSTF final recommendation applies to asymptomatic adults at average risk and recommends colorectal cancer screening for adults aged 45 to 49 years (Grade B), with screening strongly recommended from ages 50 to 75 years (Grade A). Multiple acceptable strategies are available, including annual FIT and colonoscopy every 10 years among others. Therefore C is correct. A delays screening beyond the recommended starting age, B incorrectly makes screening symptom-triggered, and D uses an incorrect annual colonoscopy interval and falsely treats one strategy as universally preferred.
educational_objective: Initiate colorectal cancer screening at age 45 for asymptomatic average-risk adults using an appropriate USPSTF-recommended screening strategy.
source_document_title: Colorectal Cancer: Screening — Final Recommendation Statement and Clinician Summary
source_version_date: May 18, 2021 final recommendation; remains listed as current USPSTF A/B recommendation in August 2026
source_locator: Recommendation Summary/Clinician Summary: adults 45-49 years — screen for colorectal cancer, Grade B; applies to asymptomatic average-risk adults age 45 or older. Implementation: several recommended tests; FIT annually, stool DNA-FIT every 1-3 years, CT colonography every 5 years, flexible sigmoidoscopy options, and colonoscopy every 10 years.
source_claim_supported: An asymptomatic average-risk 45-year-old should begin colorectal cancer screening now using a recommended screening strategy; screening is not delayed until symptoms or age 60 and colonoscopy is not recommended annually.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide age- and risk-appropriate health screening and preventive-care teaching and identify recommended health-maintenance interventions.
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — colorectal cancer screening

source_original.stem: An asymptomatic 45-year-old adult at average risk for colorectal cancer has never been screened. What does the USPSTF recommend?

options.A: Defer routine screening until age 60 because average-risk adults younger than 60 do not benefit.
options.B: Wait for gastrointestinal symptoms before screening because asymptomatic adults do not meet screening criteria.
options.C: Begin colorectal cancer screening now using one of the USPSTF-recommended screening strategies.
options.D: Begin annual colonoscopy now because colonoscopy every year is the preferred USPSTF screening strategy.

source_original.rationale: USPSTF recommends colorectal cancer screening beginning at age 45 for average-risk asymptomatic adults. Option C is correct. Screening is preventive rather than symptom-triggered, and multiple strategies are acceptable; annual colonoscopy is not the recommended schedule.
source_original.source_detail: Recommendation Summary: screen average-risk asymptomatic adults age 45-49 (Grade B) and age 50-75 (Grade A); selectively offer screening age 76-85 based on health, prior screening, and preferences. USPSTF Final Recommendation Statement dated 2021-05-18; remains the current final USPSTF colorectal-cancer screening recommendation, live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive screening, immunization, pregnancy/reproductive health and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the screening-age construct and key C after currentness verification. Tightened the stem to 'current USPSTF recommendation support' and strengthened the rationale with the actual menu of acceptable strategies and the 10-year colonoscopy interval, preserving the average-risk/asymptomatic scope.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current USPSTF final recommendation and current A/B recommendation list; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: May 2021 recommendation remains the current final USPSTF colorectal screening recommendation and is on the current A/B list, live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: USPSTF Recommendation Summary and Clinician Summary > ages 45-49, population applicability, and implementation strategies
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item is limited to an asymptomatic average-risk 45-year-old and does not generalize to hereditary syndromes, inflammatory bowel disease, or symptomatic diagnostic evaluation.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because screening starts at 45, not 60.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because the recommendation is preventive and applies to asymptomatic adults.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because colonoscopy is a 10-year screening strategy, not annual, and multiple strategies are acceptable.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C matches both the starting age and the USPSTF strategy flexibility.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are screening-policy statements for the same average-risk adult.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance — age-appropriate screening and preventive care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current USPSTF listing, recommendation population, Grade B age range, strategy intervals, all alternatives, rationale, objective, NCSBN mapping, ambiguity and cueing. C remained uniquely correct.
